title: Σφὴξ καὶ ὄφις
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 331. Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Σφὴξ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ὄφεως καθίσας καὶ συνεχῶς τῷ κέντρῳ πλήττων ἐχείμαζε.
sentences.tr: Sphēx epi kephalēn opheōs kathisas kai synechōs tōi kentrōi plēttōn echeimaze.
sentences.l: A wasp, having settled upon a snake's head and striking it continually with his sting, was tormenting him.
sentences.n: χειμάζω is properly to raise a storm on a thing; of a person it is to harass without let-up, and the imperfect ἐχείμαζε keeps the storm going. ἐπί with the accusative after καθίσας carries the motion of settling onto the head, where ἐπί with the genitive would give only the resting place.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ περιώδυνος γενόμενος καὶ τὸν ἐχθρὸν οὐκ ἔχων ἀμύνασθαι, τὴν κεφαλὴν ἁμάξης τρόχῳ ὑπέθηκε, καὶ οὕτω τῷ σφηκὶ συναπέθανεν.
sentences.tr: Ho de periōdynos genomenos kai ton echthron ouk echōn amynasthai, tēn kephalēn hamaxēs trochōi hypethēke, kai houtō tōi sphēki synapethanen.
sentences.l: And he, having become racked with pain and having no way to ward off his enemy, put his head under a wagon's wheel, and so died together with the wasp.
sentences.i: And the snake, in an agony of pain and with no way to fight off his enemy, laid his head under a wagon's wheel, and so died along with the wasp.
sentences.n: ἔχω with an infinitive is 'to be able, to have the means' — οὐκ ἔχων ἀμύνασθαι, 'having no way to fend him off'. περιώδυνος is pain all round, utter agony. Chambry prints τρόχῳ; the wheel is normally τροχός (dative τροχῷ), and τρόχος with this accent is a running or a course — the sense required is plainly the wagon-wheel, and the printed accent is left as it stands.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι τινὲς τοῖς ἐχθροῖς αἱροῦνται συναποθνήσκειν.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti tines tois echthrois hairountai synapothnēskein.
sentences.l: The story shows that some choose to die together with their enemies.
sentences.n: αἱρέομαι in the middle is to choose for oneself, to prefer. The dative τοῖς ἐχθροῖς goes with the συν- of the compound, 'along with'; the moral picks up the last verb of the story unchanged.
